references.text: Aaron and his sons were forbidden to let their hair hang loose or tear their clothes as a sign of mourning, showing the connection between unbound hair and ritual status.
The continuation of regulations concerning the leper, stating that he must live outside the camp as long as he is unclean.
The command to send all lepers out of the camp, which expands on the consequences of being declared unclean.
Miriam was placed outside the camp for seven days because of leprosy, a practical example of the law in Leviticus 13:45-46.
David went with his head covered as a sign of mourning, the same action required of the leper.
Ezekiel is commanded not to cover his beard in mourning, referring to the common practice described in Leviticus.
The prophet describes covering the lips, the same action the leper was required to do.
The ten lepers stood at a distance and called out to Jesus, in accordance with regulations that lepers must keep their distance and cry out their uncleanness.
